propositions: A write whose lock acquisition times out within the budget is permanently discarded with no retry, causing data loss when holder duration exceeds the 60s timeout.
The acquire() function computes a single deadline from timeout*attempts rather than implementing a retry loop, and both fcntl and mkdir paths use non-blocking polling without fairness guarantees.
The failure is reachable under ordinary load (holder duration 70-163s) and has destroyed multiple plan-review passes and gate attestations in production.
Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() converts terminal loss into latency; retrying only the acquisition inside acquire() before the caller's write body runs prevents double-append.
Five call sites opt into retries via write_path_retries() reading REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES (default 2, clamped [0,10]), while all other callers retain fail-fast via retries=0 default.
